nodes.summary: Two indices $i, j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ are adjacent when $j \equiv i + 1 \pmod n$ or $i \equiv j + 1 \pmod n$.
nodes.title: Cyclically adjacent indices

nodes.summary: The area enclosed by a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ is the Lebesgue measure, as a real number, of the region enclosed by $S$ (the points $x \notin S$ whose connected component in $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus S$ is bounded); it is taken to be $0$ when that measure is infinite.
nodes.title: Enclosed area

nodes.summary: For integer points $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1} \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the number of lattice points $z \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ that lie on the boundary (the union of the edges) of the lattice polygon on $v$.
nodes.title: Number of boundary lattice points

nodes.summary: For a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, the region enclosed by $S$ is the set of points $x \notin S$ whose connected component in the complement $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus S$ is bounded. For a simple closed curve $S$ this is the Jordan interior.
nodes.title: Region enclosed by a planar set

nodes.summary: For integer points $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1} \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the number of lattice points $z \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ that lie in the region enclosed by the boundary of the lattice polygon on $v$, that is, the points off the boundary whose connected component in its complement is bounded.
nodes.title: Number of interior lattice points

nodes.title: Simple polygon

nodes.summary: Given integer points $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1} \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the lattice polygon on $v$ is the polygon in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with $n$ vertices whose $i$-th vertex is $v_i$, viewed as a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: Lattice polygon

nodes.summary: Let $V \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$ be a finite set of lattice points, let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be the convex hull of $V$, and suppose that $P$ has nonempty interior. Let $I$ be the number of points of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ in the interior of $P$ and $B$ the number of points of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ on the boundary of $P$. Then the area (two-dimensional Lebesgue measure) of $P$ equals $I + B/2 - 1$.
nodes.title: Pick's theorem for convex lattice polygons

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 3$ and let $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1} \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ be integer points such that the lattice polygon $P$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with vertices $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1}$ is simple. Then the area of the region enclosed by the boundary of $P$ equals $I + B/2 - 1$, where $I$ is the number of lattice points in that region and $B$ is the number of lattice points on the boundary of $P$.
nodes.title: Pick's theorem

nodes.summary: The map $\mathbb{Z}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ sending a lattice point $(a, b)$ to the point $(a, b)$ of the real plane.
nodes.title: Lattice points in the plane

nodes.summary: Let $u, v \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ with $u_0 v_1 - u_1 v_0 \neq 0$, and let $T \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be the convex hull of $0$, $u$ and $v$. Let $I$ be the number of points of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ in the interior of $T$ and $B$ the number of points of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ on the boundary of $T$. Then the area (two-dimensional Lebesgue measure) of $T$ equals $I + B/2 - 1$.
nodes.title: Pick's theorem for lattice triangles with a vertex at the origin

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
